q: Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to _____.
e: Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to deforming forces. Several real forces can add to give the net centripetal requirement. compressing forces or shearing forces is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The study of fluids has two parts, statics and _____.
e: The study of fluids has two parts, statics and dynamics. kinematics or mechanics is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at _____.
e: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at rest. Fluid statics is about fluids at rest. motion or equilibrium is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in _____.
e: Fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in motion. Fluid dynamics studies fluids in motion; statics studies fluids at rest. rest or vacuum is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The study of the flow of liquid is called _____.
e: The study of the flow of liquid is called hydrodynamics. hydrostatics or aerodynamics is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Hydrostatics is the study of liquid at _____.
e: Hydrostatics is the study of liquid at rest. Fluid statics is about fluids at rest. flow or motion is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The volume of a liquid does not depend on pressure if the temperature is constant, hence the liquid is _____.
e: The volume of a liquid does not depend on pressure if the temperature is constant, hence the liquid is incompressible. viscous or elastic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called _____.
e: In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called streamline. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross. trajectory or vector line is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers with no mixing, such a flow is called _____ flow.
e: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers with no mixing, such a flow is called laminar flow. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. turbulent or viscous is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In steady laminar flow, streamlines _____ each other.
e: In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross each other. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross. intersect or merge into is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In turbulent flow, the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both _____.
e: In turbulent flow, the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and direction. On a circle the velocity direction keeps turning even if the speed is steady. pressure and volume or temperature and density is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the fluid to be _____.
e: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the fluid to be incompressible. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. viscous or compressible is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Internal friction in fluids is called _____.
e: Internal friction in fluids is called viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). capillarity or surface tension is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow assumes the flow has no friction, meaning _____ viscosity.
e: Ideal laminar fluid flow assumes the flow has no friction, meaning zero viscosity. A limit as Δt → 0 is the instantaneous rate, so that increment goes to zero. maximum or constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An example of laminar flow is _____.
e: An example of laminar flow is sea breeze. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. storm or whirling water is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An example of turbulent flow is _____.
e: An example of turbulent flow is storm. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing. smooth pipe flow or sea breeze is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Motor car brake oil is _____.
e: Motor car brake oil is non-compressible. highly compressible or a gas is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Gases are _____.
e: Gases are compressible. incompressible or non-viscous is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In an ideal fluid, the mass flowing in section 1 must _____ the mass flowing in section 2.
e: In an ideal fluid, the mass flowing in section 1 must equal the mass flowing in section 2. exceed or be less than is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The volume flow rate is _____ throughout the pipe.
e: The volume flow rate is the same throughout the pipe. variable or decreasing is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The equation $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$ is known as the equation of _____ for fluid flow.
e: The equation A₁ v₁ = A₂ v₂ is known as the equation of continuity for fluid flow. The continuity equation A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ keeps volume flow rate constant, so a narrower section has a larger speed. Bernoulli or Stokes is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: According to the equation of continuity, the larger the area of the pipe, the _____ is the speed.
e: According to the equation of continuity, the larger the area of the pipe, the slower is the speed. Continuity: a larger pipe area gives a slower flow speed. faster or constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: According to the equation of continuity, the smaller the area of the pipe, the _____ is the speed.
e: According to the equation of continuity, the smaller the area of the pipe, the faster is the speed. The continuity equation A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ keeps volume flow rate constant, so a narrower section has a larger speed. slower or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The equation of continuity states that the liquid entering one end of the pipe leaves from the other end with a constant _____ flow rate.
e: The equation of continuity states that the liquid entering one end of the pipe leaves from the other end with a constant volume flow rate. Volume flow rate Av is constant for an incompressible liquid in a pipe. mass or density is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the equation of continuity, $V/t$ represents the _____ flow rate.
e: In the equation of continuity, V/t represents the volume flow rate. Volume flow rate Av is constant for an incompressible liquid in a pipe. mass or weight is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: If the cross-sectional area of a pipe decreases, the speed of the liquid _____.
e: If the cross-sectional area of a pipe decreases, the speed of the liquid increases. decreases or remains constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The equation $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$ applies to an ideal fluid which must have laminar flow and no _____.
e: The equation A₁ v₁ = A₂ v₂ applies to an ideal fluid which must have laminar flow and no viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). pressure or density is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The density of an ideal fluid in the equation of continuity is _____.
e: The density of an ideal fluid in the equation of continuity is constant. The continuity equation A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ keeps volume flow rate constant, so a narrower section has a larger speed. variable or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The speed of water spraying from a hose increases by making the hose area _____.
e: The speed of water spraying from a hose increases by making the hose area smaller. A smaller nozzle area raises the exit speed because Av stays constant. larger or longer is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the equation $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$, the terms $v_1$ and $v_2$ represent the _____ of the liquid.
e: In the equation A₁ v₁ = A₂ v₂, the terms v₁ and v₂ represent the speed of the liquid. Speed is the magnitude of velocity. viscosity or volume is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The equation of continuity is a manifestation of the conservation of _____.
e: The equation of continuity is a manifestation of the conservation of mass. Continuity of an incompressible fluid keeps mass flow the same at every section. energy or momentum is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation relates pressure, flow speed, and _____ for the steady flow of an ideal incompressible fluid.
e: Bernoulli's equation relates pressure, flow speed, and height for the steady flow of an ideal incompressible fluid. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow. viscosity or temperature is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation was first derived in 1738 by the Swiss mathematician _____.
e: Bernoulli's equation was first derived in 1738 by the Swiss mathematician Daniel Bernoulli. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow. Isaac Newton or George Stokes is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation can be derived using the _____ principle to a fluid flowing in a tube.
e: Bernoulli's equation can be derived using the work-energy principle to a fluid flowing in a tube. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow. impulse-momentum or Archimedes' is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: According to the work-energy principle, the work done on a section of fluid must equal the change in total _____ energy.
e: According to the work-energy principle, the work done on a section of fluid must equal the change in total mechanical energy. thermal or chemical is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In Bernoulli's equation, the term $ho gh$ represents the _____ energy per unit volume.
e: In Bernoulli's equation, the term ho gh represents the potential energy per unit volume. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow. kinetic or internal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In Bernoulli's equation, the term $p$ represents the _____ energy per unit volume.
e: In Bernoulli's equation, the term p represents the pressure energy per unit volume. Along a streamline a speed rise is paid for by a pressure drop. elastic or thermal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's theorem states that the sum of pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy per unit volume of an incompressible, non-viscous fluid in a streamlined laminar flow remains _____.
e: The choice that completes this fact is constant. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross. zero or variable is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation applies to the steady (laminar) flow of an ideal _____ fluid.
e: Bernoulli's equation applies to the steady (laminar) flow of an ideal incompressible fluid. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. viscous or compressible is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In Bernoulli's derivation, the internal friction of the fluid flow is considered to be _____.
e: In Bernoulli's derivation, the internal friction of the fluid flow is considered to be negligible. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow. infinite or constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The work done on the fluid in Bernoulli's derivation is due to the _____ of the fluid.
e: The work done on the fluid in Bernoulli's derivation is due to the pressure of the fluid. Along a streamline a speed rise is paid for by a pressure drop. gravity or viscosity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: For a horizontal pipe where height is constant, Bernoulli's equation simplifies to a relationship between pressure and _____.
e: For a horizontal pipe where height is constant, Bernoulli's equation simplifies to a relationship between pressure and flow speed. Speed is the magnitude of velocity. viscosity or density is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In a horizontal pipe, if the velocity of the fluid increases, the pressure of the fluid _____.
e: In a horizontal pipe, if the velocity of the fluid increases, the pressure of the fluid decreases. increases or remains constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation is a relationship between pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy of a fluid in _____ flow.
e: Bernoulli's equation is a relationship between pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy of a fluid in streamline flow. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross. turbulent or static is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation requires the fluid to be non-_____.
e: Bernoulli's equation requires the fluid to be non-viscous. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow. incompressible or dense is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Bernoulli's equation applies to a _____ flow.
e: Bernoulli's equation applies to a laminar flow. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets. turbulent or rotational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The air flow moving above the top curved surface of an aeroplane wing has a _____ distance to travel.
e: The air flow moving above the top curved surface of an aeroplane wing has a longer distance to travel. shorter or equal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The velocity of air flow is _____ along the top surface of an aeroplane wing.
e: The velocity of air flow is high along the top surface of an aeroplane wing. low or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The high velocity of air flow along the top surface of a wing causes a _____ pressure above the wing.
e: The high velocity of air flow along the top surface of a wing causes a low pressure above the wing. Bernoulli: high speed goes with low pressure. high or constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The lift on the wings of an aeroplane is provided by a pressure difference where pressure is high _____ the wing.
e: The lift on the wings of an aeroplane is provided by a pressure difference where pressure is high below the wing. above or inside is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In an insect sprayer, the fast moving air causes a _____ pressure at the tip of the nozzle.
e: In an insect sprayer, the fast moving air causes a low pressure at the tip of the nozzle. Bernoulli: high speed goes with low pressure. high or atmospheric is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In an insect sprayer, the liquid rushes up through the stem because the liquid inside the container is at a _____ pressure.
e: In an insect sprayer, the liquid rushes up through the stem because the liquid inside the container is at a higher pressure. The still fluid sits at higher pressure than the fast stream. lower or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The Magnus effect is commonly associated with a _____ object moving through a fluid.
e: The Magnus effect is commonly associated with a spinning object moving through a fluid. stationary or linear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The Magnus effect produces the _____ of a spinning ball.
e: The Magnus effect produces the deflection of a spinning ball. expansion or compression is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The Magnus effect was described in 1852 by the German physicist _____.
e: The Magnus effect was described in 1852 by the German physicist Heinrich Gustav Magnus. Daniel Bernoulli or George Stokes is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: During cyclones, moving air gains speed above the roof of a house causing _____ pressure on the roof.
e: During cyclones, moving air gains speed above the roof of a house causing reduced pressure on the roof. increased or atmospheric is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: During cyclones, the roof of a house can fly away because the pressure inside the house is _____ than the pressure on the roof.
e: During cyclones, the roof of a house can fly away because the pressure inside the house is greater than the pressure on the roof. less or equal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the Magnus effect, where the velocity of air and velocity of the ball are in opposite directions, it _____ the velocity of air flow.
e: In the Magnus effect, where the velocity of air and velocity of the ball are in opposite directions, it reduces the velocity of air flow. increases or doubles is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the Magnus effect, a reduction in the velocity of air flow results in _____ pressure.
e: In the Magnus effect, a reduction in the velocity of air flow results in high pressure. low or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In the Magnus effect, where the velocity of air and velocity of the ball are in the same direction, it increases the velocity of air flow which leads to _____ pressure.
e: In the Magnus effect, where the velocity of air and velocity of the ball are in the same direction, it increases the velocity of air flow which leads to low pressure. Bernoulli: high speed goes with low pressure. high or atmospheric is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The net vertical force that the air exerts on an airplane wing is calculated using the pressure difference multiplied by the wing _____.
e: The net vertical force that the air exerts on an airplane wing is calculated using the pressure difference multiplied by the wing area. volume or thickness is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The resistance to fluid motion or internal resistance of fluid is called _____.
e: The resistance to fluid motion or internal resistance of fluid is called viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). capillarity or surface tension is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Viscosity arises when there is _____ motion between layers of the fluid.
e: Viscosity arises when there is relative motion between layers of the fluid. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). absolute or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Viscosity can be thought of as a measure of a fluid's thickness or its _____ to objects passing through it.
e: Viscosity can be thought of as a measure of a fluid's thickness or its resistance to objects passing through it. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). adhesion or cohesion is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A fluid with large viscosity resists motion because its strong _____ forces give it a lot of internal friction.
e: A fluid with large viscosity resists motion because its strong intermolecular forces give it a lot of internal friction. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). gravitational or nuclear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A fluid with low viscosity flows easily because its molecular make up results in very little _____ when it is in motion.
e: A fluid with low viscosity flows easily because its molecular make up results in very little friction when it is in motion. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). density or pressure is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The viscosity of liquids _____ rapidly with an increase in temperature.
e: The viscosity of liquids decreases rapidly with an increase in temperature. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). increases or remains constant is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The viscosity of gases _____ with an increase in temperature.
e: The viscosity of gases increases with an increase in temperature. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). decreases or vanishes is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Upon heating, liquids flow more easily, whereas gases flow more _____.
e: Upon heating, liquids flow more easily, whereas gases flow more slowly. Heating raises gas viscosity, so gases flow more slowly. rapidly or freely is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Viscosity does not change as the amount of matter changes, therefore it is an _____ property.
e: Viscosity does not change as the amount of matter changes, therefore it is an intensive property. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). extensive or additive is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Dynamic viscosity is measured by a fluid's resistance to flow when an _____ force is applied.
e: Dynamic viscosity is measured by a fluid's resistance to flow when an external force is applied. Dynamic viscosity measures resistance to flow when an external shear is applied. internal or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Kinematic viscosity is measured by the resistive flow of a fluid under the weight of _____.
e: Kinematic viscosity is measured by the resistive flow of a fluid under the weight of gravity. Kinematic viscosity is the fluid's resistance to flow under its own weight, dynamic viscosity divided by density. buoyancy or friction is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Newton's law of viscosity states that the shear stress between two adjacent layers of fluid is directly proportional to the negative value of the _____ gradient.
e: Newton's law of viscosity states that the shear stress between two adjacent layers of fluid is directly proportional to the negative value of the velocity gradient. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). pressure or temperature is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Shear stress is defined as the shearing force per unit _____.
e: Shear stress is defined as the shearing force per unit area. volume or mass is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Stokes' law expresses the _____ force resisting the fall of small spherical objects through a fluid medium.
e: Stokes' law expresses the drag force resisting the fall of small spherical objects through a fluid medium. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere as F = 6πηrv. lift or thrust is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Stokes' law was derived by the British scientist Sir George G. Stokes in _____.
e: Stokes' law was derived by the British scientist Sir George G. Stokes in 1851. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere as F = 6πηrv. 1738 or 1700 is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In Stokes' law, the constant velocity of fall is called the _____ velocity.
e: In Stokes' law, the constant velocity of fall is called the terminal velocity. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere as F = 6πηrv. initial or average is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in _____.
e: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in balance. opposition or motion is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In Newton's law of viscosity, the proportionality constant is the coefficient of _____.
e: In Newton's law of viscosity, the proportionality constant is the coefficient of viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). adhesion or capillarity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic _____.
e: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic skin. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l. solid or gas is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Surface tension is due to the attractive forces between liquid molecules called _____.
e: Surface tension is due to the attractive forces between liquid molecules called cohesion. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l. adhesion or friction is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the _____ substance.
e: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the same substance. different or opposite is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Adhesion refers to forces between molecules of _____ substances.
e: Adhesion refers to forces between molecules of different substances. same or similar is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Surface tension is the reason a _____ is able to stride along the water surface without sinking.
e: Surface tension is the reason a water strider is able to stride along the water surface without sinking. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l. stone or coin is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are able to rest on water without sinking although their _____ is higher than that of water.
e: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are able to rest on water without sinking although their density is higher than that of water. viscosity or volume is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or _____ material.
e: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or porous material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. solid or metallic is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the _____ forces between the liquid and tube material.
e: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the adhesive forces between the liquid and tube material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. repulsive or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently _____ in diameter.
e: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently small in diameter. large or wide is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The rise of water underneath the ground is an example of _____ action.
e: The rise of water underneath the ground is an example of capillary action. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. viscous or turbulent is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Water is a liquid that _____ glass capillary tubes.
e: Water is a liquid that wets glass capillary tubes. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. repels or ignores is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Mercury is a liquid that does not wet glass capillary tubes, so capillarity does not occur for _____ liquids.
e: Mercury is a liquid that does not wet glass capillary tubes, so capillarity does not occur for non-wetting liquids. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. wetting or ideal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the _____ force between glass and water is greater than the cohesive force.
e: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the adhesive force between glass and water is greater than the cohesive force. gravitational or inertial is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Water level rises in a capillary tube until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for _____ forces to overcome the intermolecular forces.
e: Water level rises in a capillary tube until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for gravitational forces to overcome the intermolecular forces. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height. electromagnetic or nuclear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
